Govind Kaka had started coming to their house in the village every Sunday. He fixed the broken hinge on the cattle shed and brought Lalit a kite. Lalit's mother, Usha, smiled more when he was around.
Lalit left the kite in its paper. He answered Govind Kaka with one word each time. At night he looked at Baba's photo on the wall and felt a tight knot. What if Baba was forgotten?
One Sunday Govind Kaka asked, "Want to fly it together?"
Lalit took a breath. "Not yet. I miss Baba. I don't want anyone to take his place."
Govind Kaka nodded. "Nobody could. We'll go slow."
Lalit said, "Thank you for the kite." He meant it, a little.

qa.q: What did Govind Kaka fix?
qa.a: The broken hinge on the cattle shed.

qa.q: What was Lalit afraid of when he looked at Baba's photo?
qa.a: He was afraid that Govind Kaka would replace Baba and that Baba would be forgotten.

qa.q: What did Lalit do that was honest and still polite?
qa.a: He said plainly that he missed Baba and wasn't ready yet, and he still thanked Govind Kaka for the kite.

qa.q: How might Govind Kaka see Lalit's cold answers?
qa.a: Govind Kaka seems to understand Lalit needs time, saying no one could take Baba's place and they would go slow.

grounding: A boy refuses his mother's new partner's friendliness, fearing he will replace his father, then says so honestly and politely and lets trust grow slowly.

I'm Vaibhav, and last year I was tired of hearing one sentence. Whenever my little brother Rinku grabbed my cricket bat or my comic books, my mother Devika said, "Share. He's younger."
It felt so unfair. I started keeping quiet and angry, and slammed my cupboard door.
One evening I finally said it. "Ma, I don't mind sharing some things. But not my bat, it cracks if he hits stones with it. And not my comics, he tears the pages. He can have my old football and my puzzle."
Ma looked at me for a long time. "That's fair. I should have asked what you think."
The cupboard door has been much quieter since.

qa.a: Devika saw it was fair and realised she should have asked first.

grounding: A child told to share because the brother is younger feels it is unfair, then explains to the mother what is not okay to lend and what can be shared.
